chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said:
"Whoever dies in the crowd on the Day of Jumu'ah, or on the Day of 'Arafah, or on a bridge, and they do not know who killed him, then his blood-money is from the Bayt al-Mal."

key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury of the Muslim polity
key_terms.زِحَامِ: a crowding or crush of people

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah if someone is killed in a crowd and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who dies in a crowded public setting when the killer cannot be identified. In such a case, the diyah is paid from the Bayt al-Mal, indicating the public treasury's role in addressing untraced wrongful death within society.
